incident-bot: paging: SLO breach detected for canary traffic -> model=redwood-v3.2-quant; metric=p99_latency; window=5m; value=3.8s (>3.0s SLO). auto-escalation to oncall.

dmitri: acknowledged. I'm oncall. severity=page. hooking in SRE + runtime.

sarah: seeing same in dashboards. p95 ~ 1.1s, p99 ~ 3.8s, errors ephemeral but streaming stalls increased. Link: https://metrics.redwood.example/canary/v3.2/overview

maria: can confirm spike started ~T-4m, coincides with rollout step: canary traffic shifted 10% at 2164506740 by deploy-bot.

ben: adding headroom: memory/KV miss rate jumped ~x3 at same time. likely cache thrash on new model parameters.

oncall-sre: can you paste the deploy details? what variant was rolled? any quant changes?

deploy-bot: Deployment event: user=eng-lead; action=traffic-shift; target=redwood-v3.2-quant; from=0%; to=10%; ts=2164506740

sarah: logs show a lot of "kv_cache_miss" and repeated ATTEMPT_RECOMPILE messages from runtime. snippet:

```
[2026-03-15T17:06:40Z] runtime: model=redwood-v3.2-quant instance=rt-07 error=kv_cache_miss key=ctx_42
[2026-03-15T17:06:41Z] runtime: kernel=matmul_opt recompile_hint=true latency=250ms
[2026-03-15T17:06:42Z] stream: stall_detected conn=stream-8 p99=3.7s
```

tara: that's consistent with a quantized kernel path thrash when new shard layout is hot. could be model variant memory layout different, causing cross-instance cache churn.

dmitri: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause canary rollout 2) divert new canary traffic to stable model variant (fallback) 3) temporarily scale up canary pool by +1 instance 4) enable KV prefill for active contexts 5) open customer-impact notes. who's doing what?

maria: taking step 1: issuing pause now.

```
# pause rollout
rwdctl rollout pause --target redwood-v3.2-quant --by=eng-lead
```

deploy-bot: rollback/pause acknowledged by orchestration -> status=PAUSED

ben: doing step 3: scaling canary pool. running:

```
infractl scale --pool canary-v3.2 --delta +1
```

oncall-sre: routing fallback: change policy to route canary-tokens->redwood-v3-stable. command:

```
routerctl update-policy --match canary=true --dest redwood-v3-stable
```

sarah: enabling KV prefill for top 200 prefixes using existing warmup job.

eng-lead: I'm starting a quick rollback decision window: if p99 doesn't improve to <2.5s within 5m after pause+reroute, we rollback to prior model image.

dmitri: I'll coordinate with support to surface to enterprise customers. severity remains page until stabilized.

ops: customer-impact: no widespread 5xx surge yet, but a few high-throughput tenants report degraded interactive latency on streaming APIs. logged as "investigating" in support portal: INC-7892

maria: after pause + reroute p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 2.6s in first 90s, p95 steady ~1.0s. still some streaming stalls but trending down.

ben: memory pressure reduced after scale up, KV miss rate halved. traces show fewer recompile hints.

dmitri: good. keep monitoring. if p99 <= 2.5s in next 3m we keep paused and run canary in reduced config. else we roll back.

sarah: FYI attaching a flamegraph link and a short trace: https://traces.redwood.example/trace/abc123

eng-lead: starting rollback window now (3m). I prefer safe rollback if any regression remains. initiating rollback plan ready.

tara: suggestion for postmortem: reproduce on test rig with quantized variant and synthetic prefix churn; likely fix is better initial KV prefill + adjusted kernel schedule.

dmitri: oncall handoff note: I'll remain until stabilized then hand to eng-sre for deeper root cause. @eng-sre please take after 2164507142.

oncall-sre: acknowledged, will pick up at handoff. preparing post-incident followups and customer comms draft.

deploy-bot: rollback candidate prepared: redwood-v3.1-stable image already certified.

maria: final -> p99 now 1.9s, p95 0.95s. streaming stalls minimal. marking mitigations effective. keeping rollout paused and opening postmortem ticket: PM-3321

dmitri: closing page in ~10m if no regression. thanks all for quick responses :clap:

eng-lead: note for postmortem: consider adding canary prefill step to rollout runbook and stricter canary SLO gate at 10% traffic.

oncall-sre: creating incident doc and handoff: https://incidents.redwood.example/2164506789

incident-bot: incident resolved -> mitigation=paused-rollout+reroute+scale; severity=page->resolved; duration=~12m.
